query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introduce a controlled ordering reaction via post-solidification annealing to induce L1₀-like nanoprecipitates within the fcc FeCoNi matrix.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase disordered fcc FeCoNi (or its high-entropy derivative) with high saturation magnetization and low coercivity (<100 Oe).
generation.intervention: Apply a tailored thermal treatment by annealing the alloy in an inert atmosphere at 500 ± 50 °C for 1–2 hours followed by rapid quenching to freeze in the nanoscale chemical ordering.
generation.conditions: Annealing must be performed under high-purity argon; temperature maintained between 450 °C and 550 °C (as guided by phase stability limits) for 1–2 hours; post-anneal quench to room temperature; magnetic measurements at room temperature and moderately elevated temperatures.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of coherent, nanoscale L1₀-like ordered domains embedded within the disordered fcc matrix, which create local strain fields and compositional modulations.
generation.mechanism: The ordered nanoprecipitates introduce enhanced local magnetocrystalline anisotropy and act as effective pinning centers for magnetic domain walls, thereby increasing the energy barrier for domain wall motion and raising coercivity while largely preserving high saturation magnetization.
generation.predicted_outcome: Coercivity is expected to increase from below 100 Oe to potentially several hundred Oe, with only modest changes (or slight reduction) in saturation magnetization relative to the untreated alloy.
generation.baseline: Untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its high-entropy variant with coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe.
generation.boundary: The microstructure must remain predominantly fcc with only nanoscale (~5–20 nm) chemically ordered domains. Over-annealing or temperatures exceeding ~600 °C risk phase decomposition or significant grain growth.
generation.uncertainty: The precise volume fraction and size distribution of the ordered nanoprecipitates may vary with subtle processing differences, and thus the exact coercivity increase is somewhat uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples from the same fcc FeCoNi alloy batch. Subject one set to the prescribed annealing (500 °C for 1–2 hours in Ar with rapid quench) and keep the control set untreated. Use TEM and XRD to verify the presence and scale of L1₀-like ordered nanoprecipitates, and measure magnetic hysteresis loops using VSM.
measurements: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) for nanoprecipitate size and density
X-ray Diffraction (XRD) for phase identification and ordering peaks
Vibrating Sample Magnetometry (VSM) to extract coercivity and saturation magnetization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed sample does not exhibit a statistically significant increase in coercivity (remaining below ~100 Oe) or if no ordered nanoprecipitates are detected via TEM/XRD, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractThe vast high entropy alloy (HEA) composition space is promising for discovery of new material phases with unique properties. This study explores the potential to achieve rare‐earth‐free high magnetic anisotropy materials in single‐phase HEA thin films. Thin films of FeCoNiMnCu sputtered on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates at room temperature are magnetically soft, with a coercivity on the order of 10 Oe. After post‐deposition rapid thermal annealing (RTA), the films exhibit a single face‐centered‐cubic phase, with an almost 40‐fold increase in coercivity. Inclusion of 50 at.% Pt in the film leads to ordering of a single L10 high entropy intermetallic phase after RTA, along with high magnetic anisotropy and 3 orders of magnitude coercivity increase. These results demonstrate a promising HEA approach to achieve high magnetic anisotropy materials using RTA.Keywords: high entropy alloy, magnetic anisotropy, rapid thermal annealing High entropy alloy (HEA) thin films are explored to achieve high magnetic anisotropy phases. Certain HEA compositions may exhibit long‐range chemical order through the emergence of multiple sublattices, analogous to high entropy ceramics,[  ] leading to so‐called “high entropy intermetallic” (HEI) compounds.[  ] Previously, transition metal alloys with high anisotropy, such as the L10 phases of FePt and FePd have been achieved by annealing of equiatomic solid solution pre‐cursors.[  ] In the case of metastable high anisotropy phases such as L10 FeNi, unconventional annealing techniques have been employed.[  ] In particular, rapid thermal annealing (RTA) of transition metal alloy films on Si/SiO2 is an effective means of inducing high anisotropy phase formation in solid solution precursors, in part due to the substrate‐induced strain.[  ] In this study, we experimentally demonstrate two thin film HEAs with large coercivity and magnetic anisotropy achieved by RTA. We show that RTA treatment of equiatomic FeCoNiMnCu thin films leads to ≈40‐fold increase in coercivity. By introduction of 50 at.% Pt, we realize an L10 HEI phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy resulting from a reduced lattice symmetry and strong spin‐orbit coupling. While the combination of saturation magnetization and coercivity for these RTA‐ treated FeCoNiMnCu films is impressive in comparison to previously reported bulk systems, the coercivity is still modest, due to the high symmetry of the cubic lattice which limits the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy. The facilitation of low‐symmetry chemical order and crystal structure combined with strong spin‐orbit coupling is in general necessary to realize strong magnetocrysalline anisotropy. To achieve these conditions in a high entropy system, we have added 50 at.% Pt to the FeCoNiMnCu alloy, employing the high entropy intermetallic design approach in search of highly anisotropic L10 ordering. Although the certainty of Pt sites reduces the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, we demonstrate below that such optimized entropy can still stabilize a single high‐entropy L10 phase.

In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.

Recently, the magnetic properties of HEAs with varying composition have been extensively investigated. The CuAl contents had obvious influence on the microstructure and saturation magnetization of FeCoNi(CuAl)x alloy, and the Ms of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 alloy increased from 78.9 Am2 kg−1 to 93.1 Am2 kg−1 by annealing at 673 K. Annealing can effectively improve the saturation magnetization of a certain constituent. Zhang et al. have prepared the FeCoNi(SiAl)x HEAs by arc-melting method and found that the electrical resistivity increased and sacrificed the magnetization with adding SiAl content, and the coercivity with a single-phase structure (BCC or FCC) was smaller than that of the two-phase structure (BCC and FCC). Therefore, the alloy components and annealing process have great influence on the magnetic properties of alloys. In addition, Chen et al. found that the electrical conductivity of FeCoNiCrAlx alloys decreased as x increasing in single-phase (FCC or BCC) regions and the electrical conductivity in duplex phase region possessed smaller value than that in single region.
